text:
alex: Quick sync — I pushed a draft load protocol for long-context experiments. goal: apples-to-apples kernel comparisons across prefill-heavy and context-mix workloads.

maria: link?

alex: https://internal/bench/protocols/seqlen-mix-v1 (proto only, not runnable)

sam: high-level — what are we controlling exactly? sequence distribution? cache state? batching?

alex: yes. 3 axes: 1) sequence length distribution (prefill-dominant, uniform mix, tail-heavy) 2) KV cache warm vs cold (full warm, partial warm by prefix, totally cold) 3) batching policy (continuous batching on/off, fixed micro-batch sizes).

jing: important: ensure model + tokenizer + quantization flags pinned. otherwise kernel selection differences look like model drift.

alex: agreed. test harness will pin model sha, quant flags, and runner config. also disabling smart routing and fallback so requests hit same instance type.

maria: how do we generate the sequences? replay vs synthetic? they behave very differently for prefill.

alex: two modes: replay-harness (replay real traffic traces with true prefix tokens) and synthetic generator (stochastic generator that samples lengths from target distribution). both use same seed to generate prompt content for deterministic KV patterns.

sam: and batching? for apples-to-apples we should enforce identical arrival patterns to the runtime. so synthetic should simulate concurrent users with poisson arrivals, then feed to the runtime but with controlled client-side queuing.

alex: exactly. generator emits arrival timestamps; harness replays them to the front-end clients. we capture actual batching decisions and kernel selection logs.

perf-bot: perf-note: add instrumentation hooks for per-token breakdown (prefill vs decode), kernel name, kernel exec time, memcpy time, kvcache hit ratio, and batch size observed.

jing: add these counters: kernel_name, kernel_version, batch_size_histogram, kv_hit_fraction, prefill_latency_ms, decode_latency_ms, device_memcpy_ms. export via perf agent every 5s.

maria: how do we compare kernels? run same trace sequentially with kernel A then kernel B on the same pinned instance, zeroing caches and restarting workers between runs?

sam: restart workers to clear allocator state but we need to be careful about residual CUDA caches. recommend full process restart and clearing CUDA cached memory between runs. document the sequence.

alex: protocol: 1) boot instance, pin model, 2) run warmup (small synthetic warmup for 30s) or skip when testing cold, 3) run trace for N minutes, 4) stop, collect metrics, restart process, switch kernel, repeat. store raw trace and metric dump for offline analysis.

maria: metric invariants: ensure same total tokens, same request ordering. if the runtime's scheduler introduces ordering nondeterminism, we should seed it or run locally single-instance to preserve order.

perf-bot: regression-detection rule idea: use % change in median prefill latency and 95th decode latency, and kv_hit change. flag if median prefill increases >5% or 95th decode >10%.

jing: discovered a regression in kernel v3.1 on a prefill-dominant trace yesterday: 1-token continuation paths slowed ~12% at p95. suspected memcpy pattern changed when enabling fused attention.

sam: did we reproduce under replay harness or only synthetic?

jing: both, but more pronounced in replay where prefixes are highly repetitive (KV hit ratio >0.9). suggests kernel sensitive to high kv cache reuse.

alex: actionable next steps: a) run isolated microbench for memmove & kv lookup paths, b) collect kernel-level flame graphs (nvprof / cupy timeline) for the prefill bursts, c) try fallback kernel (older memmove) to measure delta.

maria: for apples-to-apples numbers we should also capture cost-per-token (GPU usage time) and throughput under tail-latency SLO. include delta-cpu/gpu cycles.

sam: small note: when comparing continuous batching heuristics, ensure we exercise short inter-arrival gaps (1-10ms) and long gaps (50-200ms) so the batching windows actually differ.

jing: I'll run a sweep tomorrow: 3 distributions x 2 cache states x 3 batching configs x 2 kernels = 36 runs. will use N=10 repetitions each, capture med/p95/p99.

alex: thanks. please upload raw traces + metric dumps to s3 path and add pointer to PR. include a short summary table of med/p95 for prefill and decode, plus kv hit ratio.

maria: can we also add psi-style load curves (rps vs latency) for each kernel? helps quantify throughput cliff when prefill spikes.

jing: yes, will export rps-latency curves.

perf-bot: checklist: seed pinned, model sha, quant-opts, restart between kernels, store traces, export kernel logs, compute med/p95/p99, cost-per-token estimate.

alex: perfect. if the regression repros, we triage: create a minimal repro, bisect kernel commits, and consider adding an opt-out flag for fused path until fixed.

maria: thanks team. any blockers?

sam: only blocker is access to 80GB GPU pool for parallel runs; I'll claim 2 nodes tomorrow.

jing: noting it here so infra can follow up: @eng-infra please approve batch GPU allocation for seqlen-mix sweep. :wave:

perf-bot: run-scheduled: 1769009900 (ETA for sweep)

alex: closing thread — we'll sync next week with results.
